[[Category:Logic fallacy]]
The '''gambler's fallacy''' is the mistaken [[belief]] that past outcomes can influence futures ones in repeated occurrences of independent random events.<ref>{{#cite:Q2796}}</ref>

== Example ==

[[File:Lawoflargenumbersanimation.gif|thumbnail|Although with increasing number of trials with a fair coin, the relative frequency of heads (blue dots) to tails (red dots) tend to 1:1, there is no obvious decrease in the gap between the absolute frequencies of the two, as expected by someone believing in the '''Gambler's fallacy'''.]]

* One has just flipped five heads in a row with a fair coin
** '''Gambler's fallacy''': the next one is very likely to be a tail
** '''Reality''': always a 50-50 chance
